title.title: No Monge minimizer for three electrons
title.subtitle: Claim: a smooth density in $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose optimal three-particle Coulomb plan is never a map

plain: Three electrons in a smooth cloud: no rule fixing two of them from the first one is ever optimal

object.heading: Schematic: the engineered density, five pieces

beats.text: A central piece of mass $1/3$ and four outer pieces of mass $1/6$
Every optimal plan splits the central mass between two equally good families of triples
A map would push $1/3$ into a piece that holds $1/6$, so no map is optimal

steps: Every optimal plan splits the centre between two families of triples
A map would send a third of the mass into a piece holding a sixth
It overflows: no map is optimal, though maps get arbitrarily close

achievement.label: The Monge (co-motion) ansatz for three electrons, Coulomb cost
achievement.context: Before: optimal maps were known for two particles (Cotar–Friesecke–Klüppelberg) and in one dimension
achievement.note: The density is engineered, not physical, and the paper says so

verify.detail: Lean: the three-dimensional Coulomb case with equal infima, not the Riesz-cost extensions
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean or run the comparator

voice.text: A centre of mass one third, four outer pieces of one sixth. Plans split it.
A map would push a third into a piece holding a sixth.
